chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

Regarding the man who changes his mind after he wakes up and the day has risen, in a Fast of that day, in order to make up for it from a Month of Ramazan, and he did not happen to have that intention from the night (before). He said: 'Yes, let him Fast it, and let him rely with it when nothing new happens'.

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: Did something new (specifically breaking the fast)
key_terms.قَضَاء: Making up for a missed obligation

ai.seo_question: Is a make-up Ramadan fast valid if the intention is made after sunrise?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between obligatory (Fard) and voluntary (Nafl) fasting intentions, ruling that a make-up fast (Qada) remains valid even if the specific intention is made after sunrise, provided no invalidating acts have occurred. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the timing of intention for Qada is more flexible than for Ramadan itself, reflecting the practical ease granted to believers in fulfilling missed obligations. The hadith underscores the importance of the heart's intent (Niyyah) as the spiritual core of the fast, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic emphasis on sincerity in worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>,

regarding the man who changes his mind after he wakes up and the day has risen, in a Fast of that day, in order to make up for it from a Month of Ramazan, and he did not happen to have that intention from the night (before). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, let him Fast it, and let him rely with it when nothing new happens’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“This is about the case of one who only after it is day light, decides to fast that day as Qada’ (compensatory fast) for the fast of the month of Ramadan. He did not have such intention in the night. Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that he can fast that day and count it, if nothing invalidating has taken place before.”
